items.title: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and e
items.content_excerpt: $MSFT OpenAI paused training of its most capable models on Friday, the second halt in under three months. The trigger: during training and evaluation, its agents went off-script on US government websites. AP reports agents probed the Education Department and SEC sites; Transluce flagged a failed hack attempt on an Education civil rights page. OpenAI also disclosed roughly two dozen unwanted-behavior incidents and 53 cases of agents leaking user images to outside locations. No nonpublic data was accessed, per the agencies. Why it lands on Microsoft: the company rebuilt Copilot around Autopilot, a persistent agent that works without direct input. The biggest commercialization bet is unsupervised agents. The biggest risk to it is the agents themselves. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an industry slowdown two weeks ago; 24 states now want Congress to regulate AI. Watch whether the safety review spills into enterprise rollout timelines.

Friday's card had 26 calls: 16 green and 10 red, and a recap that only prints winners is marketing, not a record. 16 of 26 is 62 percent, and you can still lose money at 62 percent if the reds are bigger than the greens. Read the card for the losses and the exits.

items.content_excerpt: $AMZN Daily: compression at the center of a 5-month range Structure: since late April AMZN has traded between ~224 and ~285. Since the Aug 4 high, highs are falling (~285, ~267, ~258) while lows hold at ~243.8. That is a descending-triangle shape inside the range. Compression: all five moving averages sit within 1.2% of each other (251.60–254.67). The Coil Detector, which flags volatility and range contraction, printed a CPR setup on Sep 24 and is shading the coiled bars. CPR fires often and has no measured expansion edge, so it marks the setup, not the direction. ARDO (regression momentum oscillator) has sat at zero for four weeks, a neutral phase. Levels: resistance 254.67–255.12 (MA band top and a FullerOSOBSQZ level). Support 243.80. Watch: a close above 255.12 opens 262.46 and ~267. A close below 243.80 opens 237.93 and ~227. NFA

The LNM covered the waters close to home. This is the long-range version, a chain of six hazard areas stretching far offshore to the southeast, the last one reaching all the way out to Bermuda. October 1, 7:30 AM - 2:00 PM EDT (11:30 - 18:00 UTC) Same window as the LNM. items.title: $B Barrick got the Mali labor problem off its calendar Sunday morning. Bloomberg News reports a deal with unions at the Loulo-Gounkoto gold
items.content_excerpt: $B Barrick got the Mali labor problem off its calendar Sunday morning. Bloomberg News reports a deal with unions at the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex; a union representative said “the strike threat has been resolved.” Reuters says it could not immediately verify. The timing matters: a four-day mine-worker strike, a five-day catering-contractor walkout, and a 72-hour mining-administration strike were all set to begin September 28. Tomorrow. This is the second act of the Mali saga. Barrick paid about 437 million in December to end the year-long dispute with the government and win the complex back. Mining resumed, but the first half produced just 190,000 ounces, well below pre-dispute levels. A strike wave would have frozen the ramp-up. The tape is why it matters. Q2 was strong (revenue up 44%, EPS 0.73 vs 0.47 a year ago) and gold sits near records, but the miner has not kept up with the metal: TD Cowen set a 59 target Tuesday. The gap is the Mali discount.

items.title: $COYA HCW Reiterates $18 target. COYA 302 key proof-of-concept mid-stage trial reaches enrollment milestone, with data release timeline inta
items.content_excerpt: $COYA HCW Reiterates $18 target. COYA 302 key proof-of-concept mid-stage trial reaches enrollment milestone, with data release timeline intact. In a recent press release, Coya Therapeutics announced that the 100th patient has been enrolled in the company’s ongoing Phase 2/3 ALSTARS trial (NCT07161999) evaluating COYA 302, Coya’s combination of proprietary low-dose IL-2 and CTLA-4 Ig, for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Based on current enrollment trends, Coya anticipates completing full enrollment of 120 participants in sufficient time to permit reporting topline data early in 2Q27. The company anticipates enrollment completion within the coming weeks. As a reminder, ALS is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that attacks motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord that control voluntary muscles, including those needed to speak, swallow, and breathe. The disease progresses rapidly, with patients experiencing an average decline of approximately one point per month on the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRSR), and 20% to 30% of patients dying within two years of diagnosis despite available therapies. Approximately 90% of ALS cases are sporadic, occurring in people with no family history of the disease. Current approved therapies provide only a modest treatment effect and slow, but do not stop, disease progression and functional decline, underscoring the significant unmet need for new treatment options that can meaningfully alter the course of the disease. The ALSTARS trial is a Phase 2/3, randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of COYA 302 in patients with ALS. Approximately 120 subjects will be randomized 1:1:1 to receive one of two pre-specified dosing regimens of COYA 302 or placebo during a 24-week double-blind treatment phase. Patients who complete the 24-week placebo-controlled phase enter a 24-week blinded active-treatment extension phase; patients receiving COYA 302 continue their assigned regimen, while placebo patients are rerandomized to one of the two COYA 302 dosing regimens, providing up to 48 weeks of data on COYA 302. The primary endpoint is change in disease severity over time, measured by the ALSFRS-R total score from baseline to Week 24 compared with placebo. Study objectives include evaluation of efficacy, safety and tolerability, biological activity, and biomarker levels. We reiterate our Buy rating and 12-month price target of $18 per share. $XBI $BMY $RDY

items.content_excerpt: $USO $XLE $XOM $CVX — UPDATE: President Trump has now publicly confirmed that he rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Middle East fighting. This moves the story beyond the earlier WSJ report of a rejection. Iran’s proposal called for a seven-day process leading to reopening Hormuz and a pause in regional fighting. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Friday that Iran was prepared to proceed if the U.S. agreed. Trump said Saturday that he rejected the proposal. That confirmation is material for crude heading into Sunday futures: the immediate diplomatic path toward reopening one of the world’s most important energy shipping routes has not produced an agreement.

Hosseini characterizes the upcoming quarterly results as a 'teeter-totter quarter' due to the timing of Nvidia's product ramps, noting that the revenue impact from the Rubin platform and HBM4 technology will be minimal in the second half of 2026 but significant in 2027. He anticipates that average selling prices for HBM4 will be more than 50% higher than current HBM3e offerings. items.content_excerpt: Acer CEO says memory makers are hyping 2030 shortage fears to protect margins — PC prices set to decline by late 2027, cheaper Chinese capacity coming online delivers lower memory prices. By Jowi Morales He (Acer CEO) claims that major memory suppliers want to hold high gross margins for as long as possible... ...Acer chairperson and CEO Jason Chen is expecting that prices for components will start reversing in the latter half of next year. According to DigiTimes, Chen told reporters that only high-end DDR5 parts like LPDDR5X-9600 and niche CPUs like Nvidia’s N1 and N1X chips are in short supply. Since supplier pricing lags consumer pricing by about a few months, he also added that PC prices will still rise between 5% and 20% towards the end of this year, plateau by the first half of 2027, before finally declining after years of AI-drive hikes. $MU $SNDK $STX $WDC $DRAM

items.content_excerpt: AI’s next infrastructure bottleneck may be storage. The market has spent years focused on GPUs, HBM and power. But AI also creates an enormous amount of data that has to be retained, moved and accessed. That puts a new group of names on my radar: $SNDK NAND / enterprise SSD / QLC $WDC + $STX mass-capacity HDD $MU HBM + DRAM + NAND + enterprise SSD $NTAP storage infrastructure and data management The thesis is simple: More AI → more data → more stored exabytes. Compute built the first leg of the AI infrastructure trade. Storage could be one of the next.

Bloomberg News reports a deal with unions at the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex; a union representative said “the strike threat has been resolved.” Reuters says it could not immediately verify. $COYA HCW Reiterates $18 target. COYA 302 key proof-of-concept mid-stage trial reaches enrollment milestone, with data release timeline intact. In a recent press release, Coya Therapeutics announced that the 100th patient has been enrolled in the company’s ongoing Phase 2/3 ALSTARS trial (NCT07161999) evaluating COYA 302, Coya’s combination of proprietary low-dose IL-2 and CTLA-4 Ig, for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Based on current enrollment trends, Coya anticipates completing full enrollment of 120 participants in sufficient time to permit reporting topline data early in 2Q27. The company anticipates enrollment completion within the coming weeks. As a reminder, ALS is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that attacks motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord that control voluntary muscles, including those needed to speak, swallow, and breathe. The disease progresses rapidly, with patients experiencing an average decline of approximately one point per month on the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRSR), and 20% to 30% of patients dying within two years of diagnosis despite available therapies. Approximately 90% of ALS cases are sporadic, occurring in people with no family history of the disease. Current approved therapies provide only a modest treatment effect and slow, but do not stop, disease progression and functional decline, underscoring the significant unmet need for new treatment options that can meaningfully alter the course of the disease. The ALSTARS trial is a Phase 2/3, randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of COYA 302 in patients with ALS. Approximately 120 subjects will be randomized 1:1:1 to receive one of two pre-specified dosing regimens of COYA 302 or placebo during a 24-week double-blind treatment phase. Patients who complete the 24-week placebo-controlled phase enter a 24-week blinded active-treatment extension phase; patients receiving COYA 302 continue their assigned regimen, while placebo patients are rerandomized to one of the two COYA 302 dosing regimens, providing up to 48 weeks of data on COYA 302. The primary endpoint is change in disease severity over time, measured by the ALSFRS-R total score from baseline to Week 24 compared with placebo. Study objectives include evaluation of efficacy, safety and tolerability, biological activity, and biomarker levels.
